prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- There’s no single “best” site — pick the platform that fits your priorities. Briefly:
  - Airbnb: best for unique stays, lots of private rooms or host-run experiences, strong community features and more individual hosts.
  - Vrbo: best for whole-home rentals and family/group stays (fewer shared rooms, mostly entire properties).
  - Booking.com: best if you want hotels and apartments side-by-side, lots of instant-book options, or last-minute flexibility.

How to choose between them
- If you want a whole house or condo for a family/group: lean Vrbo (and check Airbnb whole-home listings too).
- If you want quirky/unique/hosted stays or experiences: lean Airbnb.
- If you want hotels and apartments mixed, wide availability and strong instant-booking: Booking.com.
- If price is key: search all three (and Google Travel / metasearch) — different platforms can show very different fees and cancellation terms.
- If you need strong consumer protections and easy refunds: compare cancellation policies. Booking.com and some Vrbo listings have hotel-like flexible options; Airbnb has Guest Refund Policy but stricter host rules.

How to find a good host (step-by-step)
1. Filter and shortlist
   - Choose whole home vs private room, number of bedrooms, amenities, house rules, pet policy, and cancellation policy.
   - Set filters for Instant Book/Free cancellation if you need flexibility.

2. Read reviews (the single most important signal)
   - Focus on recent reviews (last 6–12 months).
   - Look for repeated praise or repeated complaints (cleanliness, communication, accuracy of listing, neighbourhood noise).
   - Read the worst reviews to see how the host responded.

3. Check host credentials and listing details
   - Look for Superhost / Airbnb Plus / Vrbo Premier / “Preferred Partner” badges and high overall ratings.
   - Check host response rate/time and number of completed stays (many platforms show this).
   - Make sure the listing has many clear photos from different angles and a complete, realistic description.
   - Confirm ID verification or verified host where offered.

4. Message the host before booking
   - Ask specific questions (see the sample message below). Quick, polite, informative replies are a good sign.
   - Confirm check-in procedures, keys, parking, Wi‑Fi speed, heating/AC, and any extra fees or deposits.
   - Note: always keep communication and payment on the platform.

5. Watch the calendar and availability
   - Gaps or inconsistent availability can be normal, but an off calendar plus pressure to book fast can be a red flag.
   - If a host asks you to pay outside the platform (bank transfer, cash) — do not do it.

6. Check location and safety
   - Use the map to check proximity to transit, attractions, or risks. Read reviews for neighborhood comments.
   - Search on Google Maps/Street View to see exterior and nearby businesses.

7. Red flags
   - No reviews or very few reviews for a listing that looks professional.
   - Host asks to communicate or pay off-platform.
   - Vague description, missing photos, or inconsistent photos.
   - Host won’t answer basic logistical questions.
   - Many cancellations or one-word defensive responses in reviews.

Sample message to send before booking
Hi — I’m interested in booking [dates]. A few quick questions: is the price total shown inclusive of all fees? How will check-in work (self-check-in/meet)? Is there secure parking? Is the Wi‑Fi reliable — can you share the typical speed? Are towels/linens provided? Are there any house rules I should know about? Is the neighborhood quiet at night? Thanks — I look forward to hearing from you.

What to confirm before you pay
- Total all-in price (nightly + cleaning + service + taxes + deposits).
- Cancellation and refund policy.
- Any security deposit and how/when it’s refunded.
- Check-in/check-out times and key/lockbox details.
- Emergency contact for host/manager.

Safety and payment
- Always pay through the platform for protections and insurance coverage.
- Keep all communication on the platform in case you need to open a dispute.
- Consider travel insurance for cancellations or medical emergencies.

On-site arrival — quick checklist
- Take photos of the rental on arrival (entrance, any damage).
- Test locks, hot water, Wi‑Fi.
- Note anything that’s not as listed and message the host immediately.

Final tips
- Book with a clear cancellation policy that you’re comfortable with.
- Compare the same property across platforms — fees and policies may differ.
- If you’re traveling to a city with strict short-term rental rules, confirm the listing is legal (hosts will often mention licensing).
- For longer stays, negotiate a discount via the platform’s messaging if the host allows it.

If you tell me your trip dates, destination, group size and priorities (budget, whole home vs shared, cancellation flexibility, pets, etc.), I can recommend which site to try first and draft a custom message to send to hosts.
